design:
I held the SUBJECTIVE lane in full: shape, naming, ergonomics, design fit, and whether each deferred rename earns its cost. Sol dark is recorded; every implementation unit below therefore routes to a native Opus `implementer` or to `builder`, and that substitution is named per unit.

## 1. The shape of the phase

One unit per fleet checkout, dispatched in catalog layer order, is the whole architecture. A checkout is the writer boundary, so `one writer at a time` is per repository, not per fleet, and a layer's units run in parallel as disjoint checkouts. Nothing publishes. The only cross-checkout mechanism is a staged tarball, and the Orchestrator owns every staging action so that no unit builds or installs into a tree another unit owns.

Each checkout gets exactly one of two unit shapes:

- `breaking-<package>` — the package has work-order rows. Opus `implementer`, high effort, because every row carries a naming or shape judgment and a guide-voice edit.
- `adopt-<package>` — the package has no rows but consumes a changed dependency. `builder` on Sonnet from one template: stage, typecheck, repair what the typecheck reddens, re-run scoped gates, stop and report on any judgment call.

Two rows are not package-shaped and get their own units. `@orkestrel/guide`'s helper rename reaches every checkout's `tests/guides.test.ts`, so it runs as the wave-closing unit with one mechanical adoption pass behind it. The `Source.methods` follows-`extends` capability the audit ruled for indexeddb's parity is a `@orkestrel/guide` unit whose first real consumer is indexeddb, and it lands with the guide rename.

## 2. Naming rulings — the vocabulary this wave ships

Every open `to` in the ledger is ruled here. Where I could not name a word without reading a return type, I give the writer a derivation rule instead of a guess, which is a specification, not a deferral.

**Two rules must land in `.claude/rules/names.md` first, because they close many rows at once and stop the next campaign rediscovering them.**

- **External mirror.** An option key, constant, or wire value that transliterates an external protocol field or engine pragma into this project's casing keeps the external word order and wording, and its TSDoc names the external source. `AGENTS.md` § Design laws already carves out external values for literal unions; this extends the same principle to keys. The carve-out never licenses a name `AGENTS.md` bans outright — `kind`, `type`, `data`, `info` — it licenses only a name whose sole defect is that it is not the word this project would have chosen. This ruling closes `sqlite s18-10` (`foreignKeys` mirrors `PRAGMA foreign_keys`) and `ollama s18-09` (`keepAlive` mirrors the Ollama `keep_alive` field) as refusals, and it leaves `msg s13-02` and `s13-03` applied because `kind` and `type` are banned outright.
- **`read*` against `parse*`.** `parse*` coerces an unknown value to `T | undefined`. `read*` obtains a value from a live host object. The fleet is already converging on this: `browser s04-01` renames its `read*` coercers to `parse*` while `browser s04-02` renames its `decode*` live readers to `read*`, and `test s11-37` renames bare nouns into `read*`. Naming the distinction in the rule makes those rows one decision instead of a recurring argument.

Rulings by row:

- **contract s03-22 (`INTRINSICS`).** I read the table. Most keys already name an operation rather than a provenance, and only the descriptor, define, and prototype operations collide across the `Object` and `Reflect` namespaces. Flat renaming forces a reader to memorize invented synonym pairs (`reveal`, `declare`, `parent`) for operations whose real difference is proxy visibility. `AGENTS.md` § Design laws says that where one word is insufficient, change the shape. Ruling: keep the flat table for the `Object` and `Number` operations, and gather the proxy-visible operations under one `reflect` sub-entity — `INTRINSICS.reflect.read`, `.write`, `.members`, `.present`, `.describe`, `.define`, `.prototype`, `.apply`, `.construct`. Every leaf stays one word naming the operation, the synonym pairs disappear, and the axis is named. This overrides both prior lanes' flat amendment and the finding's full nesting.
- **contract s03-06.** Refuse the `depth` / `breadth` pair; `breadth` names nothing in the domain and a bare `depth` loses the bound. Group under `limits`, the grouping noun the fleet already uses in `MultipartLimits`: `limits.depth` and `limits.properties`. `.claude/rules/names.md` § Group options by entity.
- **contract s03-23.** `build*`, as the ledger has it.
- **sse s18-04 and ndjson s18-03.** `reset()` becomes `clear()`. Forced by `.claude/rules/names.md` § Fixed lifecycle vocabulary, which defines `clear` as "Reset state without destroying the entity" and forbids `reset` as a synonym. No taste is involved.
- **sqlite s18-11.** `exec` becomes `execute`. Forced by the same table plus the abbreviation ban.
- **console s09-07.** Take `createCaptureResult` in `factories.ts`. The function's job is to produce a `CaptureResult`, so `create{Entity}` is the rule form and the policy instrument's `create*` gate is satisfied mechanically. The alternative — taking a `CaptureInterface` parameter — destroys the ergonomics the helper exists for and makes it destroy a capture it does not own.
- **console s09-11.** Run `s09-10` first; after the alias deletion only `DEFAULT_CAPTURE_LIMIT` remains, and it becomes `DEFAULT_STREAM_LIMIT`.
- **console s09-21.** `succeed` and `fail` on `Spinner`, `fail` on `Progress`. `fail` and `complete` are not antonyms — a failed run also completes — while `completed` and the `complete` event keep meaning "the work finished", which is the derived-state separation `AGENTS.md` wants.
- **database s05-12.** `scanDriver`, beside `conformDriver` and `auditDriver`.
- **markdown s10-08.** `isFlankingWhitespace`, as both lanes have it.
- **middleware s11-04.** Delete `resolveDefaultDirectory`. A one-line delegate adds no boundary; `AGENTS.md` § Design laws, No superfluous wrappers.
- **middleware s11-06.** `MultipartErrorCode` and `MULTIPART_STATUS`. The type follows `{Entity}{Noun}` over the error entity, matching `WebSocketErrorCode` and `QualifierErrorCode`; the constant is a map from that code to an HTTP status, so `{QUALIFIER}_{NOUN}` gives `MULTIPART_STATUS`.
- **middleware s11-12 with s11-15 (`SessionInterface.data`).** These are one decision, not two rows. `data` is on the rejected-names list, so the rename is forced. Reject `values` (collides with `Map.prototype.values` and stays generic) and `store` (collides with `SessionStoreInterface`, one term for two concepts). Rule `state`: the package's own `SessionOptions<S, TState>` already calls this the consumer's state, so one concept keeps one term. Apply the retype to `ReadonlyMap` with `set`, `delete`, and `clear` mutators in the same edit, because the interface breaks once rather than twice and the mutators have a real in-package consumer.
- **middleware s11-18.** `PartHeaders.contentType` becomes `mime`, because `MultipartFile.mime` already carries that concept in this package, and because `type` is a banned discriminant word. `UploadedFileInterface` drops the suffix only if it declares no call signatures; the writer applies that test rather than the label.
- **middleware s11-23.** Refuse. `only(paths, middleware)` and `except(...)` sit in `middlewares.ts`, so no `create*` gate reaches them, and `.claude/rules/names.md` § Standalone helpers permits a one-word helper whose meaning and arguments are unmistakable. `createOnly` names no entity.
- **middleware s11-25.** Refuse. Dropping the boolean arm forces `fallback: {}` to mean "on", which is an empty-object sentinel and reads worse than the boolean at every call site. `boolean | { exclude? }` is the standard on-or-on-with-options shape.
- **middleware referral s11b-Q1a.** Refuse. The capacity option has no real consumer; `AGENTS.md` § Design laws, Minimal public API. The finiteness documentation already landed and closes the referral.
- **websocket s17-27.** `parseWebSocketCanonical`. The helper returns `boolean | undefined`, which is exactly the `parse*` contract; `read*` names a live read this is not, and `check*` reads like a guard. The writer confirms against `tests/setupPolicy.ts` whether a `parse*` name is also placement-gated, and reports if it is.
- **browser s04-11.** Keep `fail` as the class method. `error` is a noun and `.claude/rules/names.md` fixes methods as bare verbs.
- **browser s04b-05.** The client takes `CDPSendOptions` with `session` and `timeout`; the frame takes a timeout-only options type. A frame already has a session identity, so accepting a session override invites the caller to contradict the frame. Never accept and ignore a parameter.
- **browser s04b-12.** Take the peer manager: `diagnostics.profiler` as `BrowserProfilerInterface`. `.claude/rules/names.md` § Extract sub-entities.
- **indexeddb s16-17.** Two sub-entities resolve the collision cleanly. `context.stores` becomes a manager with `names`, `create(name, definition)`, `drop(name)`, and `open(name)`; `context.indexes` gets `create(store, definition)` and `drop(store, name)`. The non-word `deindex` disappears, `store` and `index` stop being overloaded verbs, and every leaf is one word.
- **interpret s12-26.** Refuse both offered symbols. `parseTemplate` already sits in `parsers.ts` after the applied row, so a throwing twin beside it is a wrapper with no boundary. Delete `createTemplate` and let the class raise its own NOTFOUND from the parser's `undefined`.
- **interpret s12-37.** Bind through the existing `Template.computations` and delete the unconditional emission. A list of aggregate names selects a different algorithm per entry, which is a behavior-selecting magic string the rules reject.
- **interpret s12-45.** Export `canonicalizeNode(value, ancestors)` and drop the second parameter from the published `canonicalize`. Contract's own spines intern into a class because contract has one; interpret's leaf does not, and inventing a class to hide a parameter is a wrapper. `AGENTS.md` forbids the hidden module helper that the third position would need.
- **mcp s01-03.** Name each moved function `create{Entity}` where `{Entity}` is the returned type's own declared name. That derivation, not a guessed word, is the instruction.
- **qualifier s16-30.** Keep `find*` for location and rename the message producers to `describe*`, as the finding has it. One prefix stops carrying two meanings.
- **qualifier s16-32.** Declare `QualifierErrorContext` in `types.ts`. A published constructor parameter takes a named type.
- **rater s17-05 and s17-06.** The lanes shared no name; `build*` settles both, and it is the prefix the fleet already chose in `contract s03-23` and `program s15-22`. `buildWorksheetFactor`, `buildWorksheetGroup`, `buildWorksheet`, `buildLineResult`, `buildEvidence`, `buildEvidenceRows`.
- **rater s17-08.** Drop `LineResult.success`. Forced by `AGENTS.md` § Design laws, Derive state.
- **sea s12-07.** Declare `ELFNoteHeader` in `types.ts` and rename the member to `total`.
- **server s14-01.** Take the `Stream` class with `createStream` as its factory and `enqueueStreamText` folded in as a method. A stream holds state, and `AGENTS.md` keeps stateful orchestration in class methods.
- **server s14-11.** `ServerError` with `ServerErrorCode`, matching the fleet's `{Package}Error` plus code union. `HTTPError` keeps `status` because an HTTP status is that entity's real domain state, not a second vocabulary.
- **server s14-12.** `computeCodingQuality`, `computeLanguageQuality`, `computeIPv6Network` (the acronym rule keeps `IPv6` capitalized because it does not lead), and `computeClientKey`.
- **terminal s12-54.** `supportsRawMode`. `is*` is reserved for a total guard, and this predicate narrows no type. Refuse the reshape lane's widening to the reduce family as outside the row.
- **terminal s12-48, s12-52, s12-55.** Apply all. `AGENTS.md` and its rules outrank existing code, so "the documentation pins the sentinel" is not a refusal ground — the `''` sentinel, the name-returning `terminals()`, and the `shutdown` synonym all fall, and the documents move with them.
- **workflow s06-03.** Delete `createDeferred` and `DeferredInterface`. `Promise.withResolvers` is native and identical; prefer native APIs, no superfluous wrappers.
- **workflow s06-24.** `IdleInterface`, and the private field becomes `#idle`. Refuse the whole-family private rename as outside the row.
- **agent s08-13.** Refuse `strain`; it is an opaque noun naming no domain state. Rule `fault`, the fleet's existing noun for a failure record. The writer stops and reports if `AgentEventMap` already carries `fault`.
- **agent s08-22.** Hold the run state in `#run` and change `#trim`. Fewer published symbols wins.
- **agent s08-23.** `framing` becomes `format`, because renaming the method to `render` frees that word and one concept keeps one term.
- **brief s13-30.** Refuse here and carry to brief's next non-breaking pass. A positional parameter rename binds no caller, so the row does not belong in a breaking wave at all, and `output` shadows a module export in the same file.
- **program s15-23.** Delete `copyJSONValue` and route its single caller to `structuredClone`.
- **toolbox s10-25.** `TerminalBridge` with `TerminalBridgeOptions`, because `Builder` is not a sanctioned role suffix and the plural type name is forbidden. The factory renames with the class to `createTerminalBridge`; the ledger's note that `createTerminalRoutes` stays contradicts `.claude/rules/names.md` § Value-level identifiers and is corrected here.
- **toolbox s10-32.** Refuse both offered names. `WORKFLOW_CHAIN_DEPTH` reads as a depth rather than a bound on one. Rule `MAX_WORKFLOW_CHAIN`: `MAX` is the qualifier, `WORKFLOW_CHAIN` names the real subject the bound applies to.
- **test s11-37.** `readStyle`, `readToken`, `readRootToken`, `readPixels`, `readContrast` under the live-read rule. For `rgba`, name by direction: `parseColor` is taken, so if it renders a color to text it is `renderColor`, and if it coerces text to a tuple it merges with the existing parser rather than getting a new name. The writer reads the signature and reports the choice.
- **guide s15-16 and s15-17.** `extractFenceImports` and `normalizeIdentifier`, as the lanes agreed. `identifierOf` combines no constituents, so the `*Of` form does not apply to it.

## 3. Rows refused, each on named rule text

`sqlite s18-10` and `ollama s18-09` on the external-mirror rule. `sqlite s18-12` on `AGENTS.md` § Design laws, One concept one term: renaming only sqlite's `transaction` creates the alternation with `@orkestrel/database` that the rename exists to prevent, and renaming database too is a rescope, because no finding was raised against database's method. `middleware s11-23` on § Standalone helpers. `middleware s11-25` on the sentinel ban and call-site ergonomics. `middleware referral s11b-Q1a` on Minimal public API. `brief s13-30` as not breaking, carried to a non-breaking pass. `toolbox s10-32`, `interpret s12-26`, and `contract s03-06` are ruled to a third position rather than refused.

## 4. Rows that conflict inside one package

The brief asked for every such pair, and these are what the ledger and work order yield.

- middleware `s11-01` is the union of `s11-02` and `s11-04`; applying all three applies the same edits repeatedly. One carrier: `s11-01`, with the other two recorded as its parts.
- middleware `s11-12` and `s11-15` both move `SessionInterface.data`, one by retyping and one by renaming. Ruled as one edit.
- console `s09-10` deletes the server alias `s09-11` renames. Sequenced, and `s09-11` shrinks to the limit constant.
- browser `s04-10` moves `fail` off the interface and `s04-11` renames it on the class. Sequenced.
- browser `s04-01` renames the `read*` family to `parse*` while `s04-02` renames the `decode*` family into `read*`. Running them in the other order collides on the source names.
- browser `s04-21`'s interning set overlaps the interfaces `s04-10` edits. Sequenced.
- interpret `s12-27`'s new manager deliberately exposes `size`, which `s12-42` renames; interpret `s12-42` and the fleet tally question are one coordinated edit inside the interpret unit.
- middleware `s11-19`'s new cursor types deliberately reuse the member names `s11-15` renames.
- agent `s08-12` and the `referral s18 ProviderDelta` row are the same rename. One carrier: `s08-12`.
- agent `s08-23` and the audit's `s08-21` ruling both rename the same vocabulary, now declared in two places. One carrier: `s08-23`, extended to the second declaration and its guide table.

## 5. Layer schedule and concurrency

Read the publish order from the catalog table after regenerating it — the committed copy names contract at `0.0.13` while the registry serves `0.0.15`, so it is stale on versions even though the layer column is derived from a dependency graph that has not moved.

Waves run L0 through L6, then the guide wave. Within a wave the units are disjoint checkouts and run in parallel, capped at three concurrent writers on this 4-CPU host: a fourth concurrent `npm test` turns timing-sensitive suites into false red, and `.agents/orchestration.md` § Writing concurrency makes the deciding re-run the Orchestrator's after the unit exits. Each wave runs in slices that report as they finish.

Between waves the Orchestrator does three things in order: commit each unit's report beside its code, stage the next wave's tarballs, and re-baseline the remaining units against what the wave revealed.

Two scheduling facts drive the order more than the layer column does:

- **`@orkestrel/guide` runs last, not in L3.** Its helper rename reaches every checkout's `tests/guides.test.ts`, which is a development dependency and cascades no publishes, but it destabilizes the harness every other unit's gates run through. Running it after L6 costs one mechanical adoption pass per checkout; running it first would make every later brief carry an unstable harness.
- **`@orkestrel/worker` cannot be proved in this phase.** Worker pins contract at the older range because queue's pin nests a second contract copy and splits `Infer`. Staging a contract tarball at worker's top level leaves queue's nested copy in place, so worker would compile against two contract surfaces — the exact duplicate-copy failure layering exists to prevent. Worker's adoption is carried to the publish wave with that reason recorded, and its unit closes as carried rather than applied.

## 6. Tarball mechanics

The Orchestrator owns every staging action; no unit packs, installs, or restores. This removes the one race the plan would otherwise carry — packing a dependency requires building it, which writes into a tree a live unit may own.

Per wave boundary, one script at `tmp/tarballs/stage.sh` performs, for each changed dependency: `npm run build` and `npm pack` from the dependency's committed tip, writing the tarball under `tmp/tarballs/`. Then, for each consumer opening in the next wave: `npm install --no-save <tarball>`, which the process re-pin wave measured as leaving `package.json` and `package-lock.json` untouched. A link is refused outright — it skips the packing, the `files` list, and the exports map, which is most of what the proof is for.

Every staging action writes a register row to `.orkestrel/campaign/fix/tarballs.md` in the same step that performs it: consumer, dependency, the range replaced, the tarball path and digest, the staging timestamp, and the restore timestamp when it comes back. A consumer sitting on an unpublished tarball with no record of what it had is a consumer nobody can restore.

Repack whenever the dependency's source moves. A stale tarball is a stale `dist/` and it is worse for being invisible.

Restore before any distribution proof and at each wave's close: plain `npm install` in the consumer returns the registry copy, because the manifest and lockfile never changed. The register row's restore timestamp is what proves it happened.

The blast-radius file is a starting point, not the breakage set. It matches symbol names inside files that import the owning package, so it reports Vitest's `describe` as a consumer of `INTRINSICS.describe` and unrelated local identifiers as consumers of `token` and `style`. Every consumer unit re-derives its true set by typechecking against the staged tarball and reading the red, and the brief says so explicitly.

## 7. How the guide, tests, and parity list move with the rename

Each row moves as one atomic edit across five surfaces, and a unit that closes a row on fewer than all five has not closed it:

- the declaration in `types.ts` first, because TTTDD binds and the contract precedes the implementation;
- the implementation and every in-package call site;
- the guide's Surface or Methods row, every fence that spells the old name, and every `@example` — `.claude/rules/documentation.md` makes every backticked API resolve to a real export in both directions, so removing a row while the export stands inverts the same bijection that removing an export while the row stands does;
- the tests that named the old surface, derived by running the suite after the rename rather than by grep;
- the `INTERNAL` parity list where the package keeps one, which is where an interned class goes when it leaves the barrel.

A prose claim about behavior gets an executed assertion, not a substring check. `.claude/rules/documentation.md` is explicit that asserting the sentence appears is not asserting it is true, and the rows that change observable behavior — the cursor value, the expansion sentinel, the key-event name, the terminal accessor — each turn a documented outcome into its opposite.

## 8. Audit shape

Per `orkestrel-falsify`: each unit's audit subject is its returned report plus the actual diff and the actual `git status --short`, stated as numbered falsifiable claims in one shared sequence per unit, with per-claim verdicts and evidence.

Every unit gets a clean-context Opus `reviewer` lane on the subjective claims — did the ruled name land, does the guide read as one vocabulary, did the parity surfaces move together — and a Sonnet `checker` on the mechanical criteria: the old name returns no hit under `src tests guides`, each new name appears in the guide, the `INTERNAL` list matches the barrel, and the register row exists with a restore timestamp. A `checker` never stands in place of a lane.

The objective lane is `analyst` on Sol. With the bench dark, no auditor has an engine the writer did not have, and that is the phase's sharpest process problem rather than a detail — it is named under Tensions with a recommendation.

The second lane runs, per the execution loop, when the first returns FAIL, when the unit's claims span both correctness and shape, or where the subject is externally driven. For this phase that means the second lane runs on `contract`, `middleware`, `browser`, `agent`, `mcp`, and `workflow` regardless of the first lane's verdict, because each carries both a signature change and a vocabulary change.

Each round's verdict goes to `.orkestrel/campaign/fix/<unit>-audit-verdict.md` and records any lane or checker that did not run.

## 9. Exit criterion

The phase ends when all of the following hold, and not when the last engine runs out of appetite.

- Every row in `work-order.md` under L0 through L6, plus every row `audit-findings.json` adds, appears in exactly one unit and ends **applied** with its gates green, **refused** with the rule text quoted, or **carried** to a named successor with its reason on the record.
- Every fleet checkout's gate chain — `format:check`, `lint:check`, `check`, `build`, `test` — passes at its own tip with the registry copies restored, proved by one independent `verifier`, not by any writer's self-report.
- Every register row in `tarballs.md` carries a restore timestamp, and no tarball is committed.
- The two rule additions stand in `.claude/rules/names.md` in scaffold's host inventory, in the commit that states them.
- No package version is bumped and nothing is published; the wave hands the fleet to the publish campaign in layer order.

## 10. What must be measured before dispatch

The brief's third unknown is the tarball chain's cost, and it is a `verifier` unit that runs before L0 opens, not an estimate. It measures, on this host and reports with each number's run: `npm run build` and `npm pack` wall time and tarball size for contract, database, and agent as the small, middle, and large cases; `npm install --no-save` wall time into a consumer plus `git status --short` proving the manifest and lockfile stayed clean; the restore `npm install` wall time; and the full gate chain's wall time for one representative package at concurrency one and at concurrency three. The concurrency-three reading is what sizes every later unit's hard cap, and the difference between the two readings is what tells the Orchestrator whether a red timing result is the subject's or the load's.
alternatives:
**Alternative A — one fleet-wide vocabulary unit per naming family, cutting across packages, instead of one unit per checkout.** The `size` to `count` tally, the `create*` to `build*` prefix, the `is*` to `matches*` predicate form, and the manager-member vocabulary each become a single unit that edits every affected checkout in one pass. This is attractive because it is exactly how a reader experiences the drift: as one inconsistent vocabulary, not as thirty package-local defects. It loses because it breaks the writer boundary that makes the campaign auditable. A unit editing many checkouts cannot be serialized against the per-checkout units, its acceptance criteria cannot close on owned files, and its gate evidence spans repositories whose dependency tarballs are staged at different wave boundaries. The design keeps the checkout as the unit boundary and carries cross-package coherence in the ruling instead — one word decided here, quoted into each brief that needs it.

**Alternative B — apply only the rows whose rule text forces them, and carry every judgment row to the next campaign.** The forced set is real and large: the lifecycle-verb renames, the banned discriminant names, the sentinel removals, the derived-state duplicate, the native-API wrappers, the type-level suffix forms. Everything resting on a chosen word — the intrinsics reshape, the session state noun, the spinner terminal verbs, the rater prefix — would wait. This wins on one axis that matters: with Sol dark, no audit lane holds an engine the writer did not, and the forced rows are the ones where an audit can check the rule text rather than the taste. It loses on cost. Every carried row is a second breaking wave over the same published surfaces, and `AGENTS.md` is greenfield with no compatibility shims, so a consumer pays the migration twice for one vocabulary. I recommend against it as the plan, and recommend it as the fallback if the Codex bench cannot be recovered before L2 opens — which is where the judgment density rises sharply.

tensions:
**The audit cannot hold an engine the writer did not.** Sol is dark, every implementation unit is Opus, and every audit lane would be Opus. `.agents/orchestration.md` § Orchestration by harness makes the fix-round auditor an engine that did not write the work, and this phase — dozens of judgment-heavy breaking units — is the exact case that rule exists for. A clean-context `reviewer` plus a Sonnet `checker` is the strongest substitute available and it is not the same thing. My recommendation: run the login ladder for the Codex bench in the same turn the plan is surfaced, hold L2 until it returns, and if it cannot be recovered, fall back to Alternative B and apply only the rule-forced rows. The Orchestrator rules.

**Extending a vocabulary beyond its flagged rows is a rescope, and stopping at them leaves alternation.** The `size` to `count` tally is flagged in template, brief, and interpret; the same drift stands unflagged in program, middleware, msg, and pool. The toolbox code-helper family is the same shape: one member is in the row and its siblings are not. Applying the flagged subset makes the fleet inconsistent where it is uniform today, and applying the whole family moves the exit criterion, which needs the user. My recommendation: ask the user once, before the tally unit dispatches, to extend those two families whole. I did not extend them on my own authority.

**I overrode both prior lanes on the intrinsics table.** They converged on renaming the colliding keys flat; I ruled a `reflect` sub-entity instead, on the grounds that inventing distinct words for operations whose real difference is proxy visibility makes a reader memorize synonyms. This moves more published keys than the flat rename would. Challenge it if you think a flat table with distinguishing words is reachable — neither lane produced those words, which is my evidence that it is not.

**I refused rows both lanes wanted applied.** `middleware s11-23` (`only` and `except` keep their names), `middleware s11-25` (the boolean fallback arm stands), `sqlite s18-12` (`transaction` stands fleet-wide), and `middleware referral s11b-Q1a` (no capacity option). Each refusal names its rule, and each trades naming conformance for call-site ergonomics or for fleet-wide term unity. The objective lane will read the same rules and may weigh them the other way.

**I invented a rule to close two rows.** The external-mirror rule closes `sqlite s18-10` and `ollama s18-09` and forecloses the next argument of that shape. Its cost is a scaffold host-inventory change that propagates only at the next scaffold release, so this wave's units get the text quoted into their briefs rather than vendored into their trees. If the Orchestrator judges the rule addition out of scope, both rows revert to open naming questions and the ollama row's own note already asks for a fleet-level ruling.

**I moved `@orkestrel/guide` out of its layer.** Its rename is a development dependency with no publish cascade, and running it in L3 destabilizes the harness every later unit's gates run through. Running it last costs one mechanical pass per checkout. Someone weighing wall-clock over harness stability would put it first.

**I ruled `brief s13-30` out of the breaking wave entirely** because a positional parameter rename binds no caller. The work order deferred it as breaking. If the objective lane holds that moving the `.d.ts` signature text is itself the break, the row returns to the brief unit.

**Guide-documented behavior is not a refusal ground.** I applied `terminal s12-48`, `s12-52`, `s12-55`, and `indexeddb s16-15` over documentation that pins the current behavior, on `AGENTS.md` § Authority — the rules outrank existing code, and a document is code's account of itself. Several work-order rows deferred exactly on that ground.
risks:
**The blast-radius file over-reports and no unit should plan from it.** It matches symbol names inside files that import the owning package, so Vitest's `describe` global reports as a consumer of `INTRINSICS.describe`, and unrelated local identifiers report as consumers of `token`, `style`, `value`, `keys`, and `count`. A unit sizing its work from that file will chase edits that do not exist and miss ones the file cannot see, because a re-export or a type-only alias carries no matching token. Evidence that settles it: each consumer unit runs `npm run check` against the staged tarball and reports the red as its work list, which is a run rather than a reading.

**The catalog table is stale on versions.** It records contract at `0.0.13` while the brief's measurement puts `0.0.15` on the registry with every dependent except worker re-pinned. The layer column is derived from a dependency graph that has not moved, so the schedule holds, but `.agents/orchestration.md` § Publishing the fleet requires regenerating the table before sequencing a cascade. Evidence: run `scaffold catalog` and compare the layer column against the one this plan used.

**Worker cannot be proved and I planned it as carried rather than discovering it mid-wave.** Its older contract pin plus queue's nested copy means a staged contract tarball puts two contract surfaces in one tree, which the compiler reads as distinct types. Evidence: stage the tarball in a scratch copy and read the `check` output; if it typechecks, the assumption is wrong and worker rejoins L4.

**Concurrency turns timing-sensitive suites red on this host.** Four CPUs, a probe suite already red on pristine main for language-server deadlines, and three concurrent gate chains is where a wave sits. Any timing failure a unit reports is a question, and the deciding re-run belongs to the Orchestrator after the unit exits. Evidence: the `chain-probe` unit's concurrency-one and concurrency-three readings, taken before L0 opens.

**A tarball goes stale the moment its dependency's tree moves.** A fix round applied to a dependency after its layer closed leaves every consumer green against a surface that no longer exists, and the failure is invisible until the publish wave. Mitigation: repack at every wave boundary, and record the digest in the register row so a stale stage is detectable rather than assumed away.

**A distribution proof run against a staged tarball proves the tarball.** Every gate that reads the packed artifact runs after the restore, and the register row's restore timestamp is what proves the restore happened. Evidence: `git status --short` clean for `package.json` and `package-lock.json` in every consumer at each wave close.

**The two rule additions bind the writers before the vendored copies carry them.** A unit reading its target's vendored `.claude/rules/names.md` will not see the external-mirror rule until scaffold publishes and each target repairs, and no package publishes in this phase. A unit that misses it will rename `foreignKeys` or `keepAlive`. Mitigation: quote the rule text into every brief that depends on it, and never rely on the vendored copy inside this wave.

**Several rulings rest on a name I could not verify against a return type.** `mcp s01-03`, the `rgba` target in `test s11-37`, the `agent s08-13` event noun, and `terminal s12-59`'s entity are specified as derivation rules rather than words. Each carries an explicit stop-and-report instruction. The risk is that a writer treats a derivation rule as a licence to choose freely; the acceptance criteria require the report to name the signature that decided each one.

**The refusals are the rows most likely to come back.** A refusal that names its rule is auditable, but nothing in this campaign's exit criterion prevents a later round from re-raising `foreignKeys` or `only` as fresh drift. Mitigation: land the external-mirror rule and record the ergonomic refusals in each package's guide as ruled rather than overlooked, so the next scan reads a decision instead of a defect.
